events.title: The first revelation
events.summary: Aisha's report places the beginning of revelation in the cave of Hira, following a period of meaningful dreams and seclusion.
events.uncertainty: The report supplies the setting; the CE year is conventional and approximate.

passages.arabic:
ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ
خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ
ٱقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ ٱلْأَكْرَمُ
ٱلَّذِى عَلَّمَ بِٱلْقَلَمِ
عَلَّمَ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ
passages.translation:
Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth,
Createth man from a clot.
Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous,
Who teacheth by the pen,
Teacheth man that which he knew not.

events.title: Khadija offers reassurance
events.summary: After the experience at Hira, Khadija reassured the Prophet ﷺ by recalling his care for relatives, guests, and people in difficulty.
events.uncertainty: A sequence within the first-revelation report, rather than a separately dated event.

events.title: A conversation with Waraqa
events.summary: Khadija brought the account to Waraqa ibn Nawfal, who connected the experience with earlier revelation and anticipated opposition.
events.uncertainty: The report describes the sequence without a calendar date.

events.title: Revelation after a pause
events.summary: Jabir's report describes revelation resuming after a pause and associates the moment with the opening instructions of Al-Muddaththir.
events.uncertainty: Exact length of the pause and CE date are not established here.

events.title: Calling the clans at Safa
events.summary: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet ﷺ gathered the clans at Safa and warned them publicly. Their answer acknowledged his previous truthfulness.
events.uncertainty: Commonly placed in the early public mission; the report itself gives no CE year.

events.title: Khabbab asks for help
events.summary: Khabbab recalled asking for help during persecution. The reported reply placed their suffering alongside the endurance of earlier believers.
events.uncertainty: A broad Makkan placement is used because this report does not date the exchange.

events.title: Abu Bakr and protection
events.summary: Aisha's report describes Ibn al-Daghina offering Abu Bakr protection, disputes about public worship, and Abu Bakr later releasing him from that agreement.
events.uncertainty: The episode predates the Hijrah, but the precise CE year is not supplied.

events.title: A difficult encounter and a merciful response
events.summary: When recalling a painful rejection, the Prophet ﷺ described declining an offer of destruction and hoping for future generations who would worship Allah.
events.uncertainty: Often associated with the Taif journey. The report names locations but gives no CE date.

events.title: The Night Journey and ascent
events.summary: The report of Malik ibn Sasaa describes the Night Journey and ascent, including the prescription of prayer.
events.uncertainty: The exact date is disputed. Its position here is a broad pre-Hijrah placement, not a fixed anniversary.

events.title: The pledges at Aqabah
events.summary: Ubada ibn al-Samit is identified as an Aqabah participant and reports a pledge covering worship and conduct.
events.uncertainty: This report identifies a participant and a pledge; it does not by itself establish every detail of the two Aqabah meetings.

events.title: The cave during the migration
events.summary: Abu Bakr recalls concern that pursuers might see them in the cave and the Prophet's ﷺ reassurance. Quran 9:40 also refers to the two in the cave.
events.uncertainty: The Hijrah is conventionally dated to 622 CE. The report quoted here does not name the cave.

passages.arabic: إِلَّا تَنصُرُوهُ فَقَدْ نَصَرَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِذْ أَخْرَجَهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ثَانِىَ ٱثْنَيْنِ إِذْ هُمَا فِى ٱلْغَارِ إِذْ يَقُولُ لِصَـٰحِبِهِۦ لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَنَا ۖ فَأَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ سَكِينَتَهُۥ عَلَيْهِ وَأَيَّدَهُۥ بِجُنُودٍ لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا وَجَعَلَ كَلِمَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ ٱلسُّفْلَىٰ ۗ وَكَلِمَةُ ٱللَّهِ هِىَ ٱلْعُلْيَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
passages.translation: If ye help him not, still Allah helped him when those who disbelieve drove him forth, the second of two; when they two were in the cave, when he said unto his comrade: Grieve not. Lo! Allah is with us. Then Allah caused His peace of reassurance to descend upon him and supported him with hosts ye cannot see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the nethermost, while Allah's Word it was that became the uppermost. Allah is Mighty, Wise.

events.title: Suraqa on the route
events.summary: Suraqa's account describes pursuing the travelers, his horse stumbling, and his eventual request for a written assurance of safety.
events.uncertainty: The report supplies the episode; this schematic view does not reconstruct the exact route.

events.title: Arrival among Banu Amr ibn Awf
events.summary: Anas reports an initial stay among Banu Amr ibn Awf, followed by a welcome from Banu al-Najjar and arrival at Abu Ayyub's courtyard.
events.uncertainty: Relative sequence is clearer than an exact Gregorian day.

events.title: Building the mosque
events.summary: Anas describes preparing a site for the mosque in Madinah and the community's involvement in the work.
events.uncertainty: Shown after arrival. The cited report is the evidence for the construction episode.

events.title: Brotherhood and a market
events.summary: The report pairs Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf with Sad ibn al-Rabi. It records Sad's generous offer and Abd al-Rahman's request to be shown the market.
events.uncertainty: The report places the episode after the emigrants reached Madinah; no exact date is supplied.

events.title: The change of qiblah
events.summary: Al-Bara reports prayer toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, followed by the change toward the Kaaba.
events.uncertainty: The narrator preserves a sixteen-or-seventeen-month uncertainty; the app keeps that uncertainty.

passages.arabic: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَىٰهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ ٱلْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنتُمْ فَوَلُّوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُۥ ۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ
passages.translation: We have seen the turning of thy face to heaven (for guidance, O Muhammad). And now verily We shall make thee turn (in prayer) toward a qiblah which is dear to thee. So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces (when ye pray) toward it. Lo! Those who have received the Scripture know that (this revelation) is the Truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.

events.title: Supplication at Badr
events.summary: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet's ﷺ earnest supplication at Badr and Abu Bakr's presence. Quran 3:123 explicitly names Badr.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is a chronology aid. The report is cited for the supplication, not a complete battle narrative.

passages.arabic: وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ وَأَنتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ ۖ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
passages.translation: Allah had already given you the victory at Badr, when ye were contemptible. So observe your duty to Allah in order that ye may be thankful.

events.title: The archers at Uhud
events.summary: Al-Bara describes the instructions given to the archers under Abdullah ibn Jubayr and the consequences of leaving their position.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is approximate in CE terms; details follow the named report.

events.title: A report on the retreat
events.summary: A second report from Al-Bara identifies the archers' commander and recalls the retreat during Uhud.
events.uncertainty: A separate report about the same battle, not another battle or an independently dated event.

events.title: Digging the trench
events.summary: Anas recalls the emigrants and helpers carrying earth while digging the trench, with hunger and difficult food supplies during the work.
events.uncertainty: The trench campaign is conventionally placed in 5 AH; the cited report describes the labor.

events.title: The account of the slander
events.summary: Aisha's extended report recounts the false accusation against her and the distress and eventual resolution that followed.
events.uncertainty: Its relation to some campaigns is debated. Placement in this band is approximate, not a claim of a precise year.

events.title: The journey to Hudaybiyah
events.summary: Al-Miswar and Marwan's account describes a journey intended for Umrah, negotiations with Quraysh, and the eventual agreement.
events.uncertainty: Conventional 6 AH placement. The linked report contains the detailed sequence.

events.title: The pledge beneath the tree
events.summary: Jabir recalls the group at Hudaybiyah and identifies the tree associated with the pledge. Quran 48:18 explicitly mentions the pledge beneath a tree.
events.uncertainty: Jabir gives a group count in this report. Other transmitted counts should not be silently harmonized.

passages.arabic: ۞ لَّقَدْ رَضِىَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحْتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ فَأَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَثَـٰبَهُمْ فَتْحًا قَرِيبًا
passages.translation: Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance unto thee beneath the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down peace of reassurance on them, and hath rewarded them with a near victory;

events.title: Negotiating the written agreement
events.summary: The Hudaybiyah account records negotiations and the writing of treaty terms. Its difficult concessions form part of the report's sequence.
events.uncertainty: A detail of the same treaty episode, not a separate treaty.

events.title: The banner at Khaybar
events.summary: Sahl ibn Sad reports the announcement about the banner at Khaybar and its being given to Ali ibn Abi Talib.
events.uncertainty: The conventional year is shown; the linked report supports the banner episode.

events.title: A letter and questions from Heraclius
events.summary: Abu Sufyan's account describes Heraclius questioning him during the truce with Quraysh and a letter from the Prophet ﷺ.
events.uncertainty: The report explicitly situates the exchange during the truce. The CE placement is approximate.

events.title: The return for Umrah
events.summary: Al-Bara's report describes the agreement for a later visit to Makkah and a stay of three days under its terms.
events.uncertainty: The report links the visit to the agreement; its conventional chronology is 7 AH.

events.title: The approach to Makkah
events.summary: The report describes the approach during the year of the conquest and Abu Sufyan's encounter with the Muslim camp.
events.uncertainty: The year of the conquest is explicit in the report. CE conversion is approximate.

events.title: The Kaaba at the conquest
events.summary: Abdullah reports the removal of idols around the Kaaba when the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah.
events.uncertainty: A detail of the conquest episode. No depictions of the Prophet ﷺ are used.

events.title: Steadfastness at Hunayn
events.summary: Al-Bara reports that the Prophet ﷺ did not flee at Hunayn, while some people hurried away under the opposing archers' attack.
events.uncertainty: The conventional placement follows the conquest; the report supports this specific observation.

events.title: The expedition to Tabuk
events.summary: Kab ibn Malik's account describes his failure to join the expedition to Tabuk and the circumstances that followed.
events.uncertainty: Shown in the conventional 9 AH band. Read the complete report for its longer sequence.

events.title: Kab ibn Malik tells the truth
events.summary: Kab's account contrasts his truthful admission with the excuses he might have offered and recounts the eventual acceptance of repentance.
events.uncertainty: Part of the same report as Tabuk. Its relative sequence is more important here than an exact CE day.

events.title: Announcements during Abu Bakr's Hajj
events.summary: Abu Hurayra recalls being sent among the announcers at the Hajj led by Abu Bakr. The report also mentions Ali reciting Baraah.
events.uncertainty: Conventionally placed in 9 AH, before the Prophet's ﷺ Farewell Hajj.

events.title: The Farewell Hajj
events.summary: Jabir's long report describes the announced pilgrimage in the tenth year, its journey, rites, and the address at Arafat.
events.uncertainty: The report explicitly identifies the tenth year in Madinah. Individual Gregorian date conversions are not asserted.

events.title: Conveying the message
events.summary: Abu Bakra reports an address on the Day of Nahr emphasizing the sanctity of life and property and conveying the message to those absent.
events.uncertainty: This report concerns the address at Mina; it is not silently merged with every other Farewell Hajj sermon.

events.title: The death of the Prophet ﷺ
events.summary: Aisha describes his final moments in her home. Another report records Abu Bakr addressing the community afterward and reciting Quran 3:144.
events.uncertainty: The year is conventional. The report supports the setting of the final moments; see the additional report for the community response.

passages.arabic: وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ ۚ أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَـٰبِكُمْ ۚ وَمَن يَنقَلِبْ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَن يَضُرَّ ٱللَّهَ شَيْـًٔا ۗ وَسَيَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلشَّـٰكِرِينَ
passages.translation: Muhammad is but a messenger, messengers (the like of whom) have passed away before him. Will it be that, when he dieth or is slain, ye will turn back on your heels? He who turneth back on his heels doth no hurt to Allah, and Allah will reward the thankful.

dailyPairs.why: The Waraqa conversation belongs to the report of the beginning of revelation, and the public call at Safa came in the mission that followed.
Khadija's reassurance is part of the report of the beginning of revelation, and the Aqabah pledges came shortly before the Hijrah.
The call at Safa belongs to the early Makkan mission, and the cave belongs to the Hijrah that ended the Makkan period.
Khabbab's request is a Makkan-period exchange, and the arrival among Banu Amr ibn Awf happened after the migration to Madinah.
The report on Abu Bakr and protection describes a time before the Hijrah, and Badr was fought in Madinah in 2 AH.
The Aqabah pledges came before the Hijrah, and the qiblah was changed in Madinah in 2 AH.
The cave was part of the Hijrah, and the report on the qiblah counts months of prayer toward Jerusalem after the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah.
Suraqa met them on the road of the Hijrah in 1 AH, and Badr took place in 2 AH.
In Bukhari 428 the Prophet ﷺ stays among Banu Amr ibn Awf, then sends for Banu al-Najjar and has the mosque built.
The brotherhood of the emigrants and helpers belongs to the first Madinan period, and Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
